% References to labels of another document with xr-hyper, from an .aux
% that LaTeX wrote under hyperref, with no .xref beside it. Each prints
% its number, page, or name as in the PDF, as does a label from an .aux
% that LaTeX wrote without hyperref. \autoref prints its name and no
% link to this document's theorem with the same anchor, and \hyperref
% its text. A label of an .aux that tex4ht wrote under hyperref links to
% that document's page, and a label of this document to its heading.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\usepackage{xr-hyper}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}
\externaldocument[P-]{test-xr/plain}
\externaldocument[H-]{test-xr/hyper4ht-hyper}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
Starred \ref*{X-s}. Section \ref{X-ss}. Page \pageref{X-front}.
Item \ref{X-item}. Bold \ref{X-emph}. Empty [\ref{X-none}].
Named \nameref{X-thm}. Named in italics \nameref{X-emph}.
Spaced \ref{X-step}. Included \ref{X-c}.
Auto \autoref{X-thm}. Cleveref's \ref{X-emph@cref}.
Auto section \autoref{X-ss}. Auto starred \autoref*{X-thm}.

Without hyperref: subsection \ref{P-ss}, page \pageref{P-front}.
Auto written by tex4ht \autoref{H-oss}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.

\begin{theorem}
The first theorem of this document.
\end{theorem}

% (last: tex4ht's \hyperref leaves its text defined, for xr's links after it
% to an .aux that tex4ht wrote)
Hyperref \hyperref[X-ss]{text}.
Hyperref around \hyperref[X-ss]{see \ref{X-s}}.
Local around \hyperref[here]{see \ref{X-ss}}.
After \ref{X-ss}.
\end{document}
